title: ISO and India — BIS, NABL, and the National Standards Ecosystem
shortDescription: How ISO's international standards actually connect to India's own standards and accreditation bodies — and why BIS, NABL, and NABCB are not the same thing.
genZNote: ISO writes the world's rulebook; BIS adapts it for India; NABL checks who's actually following it.

sections.heading: BIS — Bureau of Indian Standards
bullets: India's NATIONAL STANDARDS BODY — India's representative member at ISO (and at IEC), established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (BIS itself traces back to the earlier Indian Standards Institution, founded 1947).

Develops Indian Standards (IS), often by adopting or adapting relevant ISO/IEC international standards to Indian conditions, and administers product certification (the ISI mark) and the Hallmarking scheme for precious metals.
BIS is the body that ADOPTS/ADAPTS international standards for India — it does not itself write ISO's international standards, though its experts do participate in ISO technical committees.

rows: An apex national body (set up as a public-private partnership) that houses several accreditation boards, including NABCB.
NABCB — National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies
Accredits CERTIFICATION bodies (those that certify organizations against management-system standards like ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 22000, ISO/IEC 27001).
NABL — National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories
Accredits TESTING, CALIBRATION, and MEDICAL laboratories specifically — i.e. the body relevant to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 accreditation in India.

sections.heading: Do Not Merge These Roles
bullets: BIS sets/adapts STANDARDS for India and runs its own certification schemes (like the ISI mark) — it is India's national standards body, comparable to ISO membership status.
NABL accredits LABORATORIES specifically (testing, calibration, medical) against ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 — it does not set standards itself.
NABCB accredits CERTIFICATION BODIES that certify organizations against management-system standards like ISO 9001 — a different layer again from NABL's laboratory-specific role.

A laboratory can be 'NABL-accredited' (meaning NABL has confirmed its competence against ISO/IEC 17025 or ISO 15189) — this is separate from BIS product certification and separate again from NABCB's role certifying management-system certification bodies.

sections.heading: The Full Chain, India Edition
sections.body: ISO (writes the international standard) → BIS (adopts/adapts it as an Indian Standard, and participates in ISO's technical committees) → an independent certification body (certifies a specific organization against the standard) → NABCB or NABL (accredits that certification/testing body as competent to do so). Government regulation, where it applies, then mandates specific certifications in specific regulated sectors (e.g. certain electronics, toys, and food-contact materials require BIS certification by law in India).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: BIS is India's national standards body (ISO/IEC member for India); NABL accredits testing/calibration/medical laboratories; NABCB accredits certification bodies for management-system standards — three distinct roles in India's conformity ecosystem.
keyFacts: BIS: India's ISO/IEC member body, HQ New Delhi, established under the BIS Act, 1986 (predecessor: Indian Standards Institution, 1947).
NABL: accredits testing, calibration, and medical laboratories (relevant to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189).
NABCB: accredits certification bodies for management-system standards (relevant to ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, 22000, 27001).
Both NABL and NABCB operate under the Quality Council of India (QCI).
commonConfusion: BIS sets/adapts standards and runs its OWN certification (ISI mark); NABL and NABCB are ACCREDITATION bodies for OTHER certifiers/labs — do not merge BIS's role with NABL's or NABCB's.

highYieldFacts: BIS is India's representative national standards body at ISO — established under the BIS Act, 1986.
NABL accredits laboratories; NABCB accredits certification bodies — these are two separate accreditation streams under QCI.
'NABL-accredited' relates specifically to ISO/IEC 17025 (testing/calibration) or ISO 15189 (medical) laboratory accreditation.
commonTraps: Do not say 'BIS accredits laboratories' — that is NABL's role; BIS sets/adapts standards and runs its own product certification (ISI mark).
Do not say 'NABL certifies companies against ISO 9001' — NABCB, not NABL, is the accreditation body relevant to management-system certification bodies.
mustRemember: BIS traces back to the Indian Standards Institution (1947), formalised as BIS under the 1986 Act.
NABL and NABCB both sit under the Quality Council of India (QCI).

confusedTerms.distinction: NABL accredits testing, calibration, and medical LABORATORIES (ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189); NABCB accredits CERTIFICATION BODIES that certify organizations against management-system standards like ISO 9001.
